1.grade_note: Simple narrative, clear theme; fine for grade 6, on the easy side.
1.free_elimination: A uses an absolute ('always'); D and C are generic morals with weak passage hooks.
1.note: Clean. A is a reasonable trap (she worked hard and failed).

2.free_elimination: A and B claim first-person access the narrator plainly lacks (Lucia's thoughts; box opened), eliminable from general POV knowledge; C is a hedgeless certainty claim.
2.note: Option B says 'himself' but the narrator's gender is never stated; use 'the narrator opens it'.

3.free_elimination: Options pair into two openings (Pepper runs off / Kofi takes Pepper); C is visibly incomplete (no resolution), so a summary-savvy student narrows to A vs B without reading closely.
3.note: B and D add invented details; easy item.

4.free_elimination: D is visibly a narrow detail; B introduces cleaning/safety, unrelated to the dance framing.

5.free_elimination: C contradicts the author's evident position; D is trivial.
5.note: Very easy: the Riverton sentence directly follows 'Some people argue that a garden would cost too much. However,' so the signal word hands over the answer. Probably below 200.

6.free_elimination: A and B are literal light/color senses, implausible for a person in a class context; C contradicts 'quiet'.

7.free_elimination: C and D are common senses unrelated to a bridge's condition.
7.note: B 'sensible' is a good trap (sound judgment).

8.note: Slow-on-land vs strong-swimmer contrast is very obvious; likely below 200.

9.grade_note: 'Creaked' for wooden stairs is roughly grade 3-4 word choice, not grade 7.
9.free_elimination: Buzzed and splashed are absurd for stairs without any skill; chimed nearly so.
9.note: Distractors are not attractive; no real student at grade 7 would choose B or C.

11.free_elimination: C and D are obvious fragments by shape; A and B differ only by 'so', making the key the 'complete' version of B.
11.note: Minor: 'opens' (present) with 'got' (past) is slightly odd but acceptable.

12.grade_note: Agreement across a prepositional phrase with plural noun; grade 7 fine.
12.free_elimination: Options split into singular/plural x present/past; the plural pair is the trap, the tense choice decides.
12.note: 'The list ... was taped to the refrigerator door, and Mom checks it every night' is defensible (past placement event, present habit). The item relies on tense consistency that is not strictly required. Use a frame that forces present tense, or drop 'was'.

13.free_elimination: B starts with lowercase 'my', which any student rejects. Key is the per-token majority of the option set (My, uncle, Aunt, river each appear in 3 of 4).
13.note: Single-deviation distractor design: each distractor differs from the key in exactly one token.

14.grade_note: Days, months, seasons; fine for grade 6.
14.free_elimination: Per-token majority (Monday, June, summer each 3 of 4) identifies A without knowing any rule.
14.note: Lowercase 'monday'/'june' are errors few grade 6 students would miss; only 'Summer' is a live trap. Likely below 190.

15.grade_note: Region vs direction, appropriate for grade 6-7.
15.free_elimination: Per-token majority (South, town, north each 3 of 4) yields D.
15.note: 'Town' capitalization is an implausible error; region/direction is the real skill.

16.free_elimination: Per-token majority (Journey, to, Edge, Sea) yields B. C's lowercase first word is implausible.
16.note: Real book titles may exist with this name; title should ideally be italicized/underlined, though for a capitalization item it's tolerable.

17.free_elimination: Per-token majority (up, Lena, or) yields D; B's lowercase name is an implausible error.
17.note: Only C ('Or') tests the actual skill; 220-229 is high for an item with two dead distractors.

18.grade_note: Title-before-name vs generic title is a good grade 8-9 rule.
18.free_elimination: Per-token majority (governor, Senator, senators) yields B.
18.note: Skill is appropriately hard, but the majority tell makes it far easier than 230-239 for a test-wise student.

19.free_elimination: Key shares the most letters/patterns with the other three (consensus spelling).
19.note: Far too easy for grade 5; even 180-189 is generous.

20.grade_note: Consonant doubling in 'swimming' is a grade 2-3 rule.
20.free_elimination: B (triple m) and C ('swimeing') are implausible; A vs D is the only live choice.

21.free_elimination: B, C, D are all common correctly spelled words; 'colum' visibly looks truncated.
21.note: Silent letters theme is fine but the target is too easy for grade 7/200-209.

22.free_elimination: B and D (-ibal, -ibel) are implausible; key is the consensus of root+suffix patterns.
22.note: Only A is a real trap; probably below 210.

23.free_elimination: Consensus: 'persev-' in 3 of 4, '-ance' with c in 2 of 4; the key is the only option with no deviation from the majority pattern. C '-anse' is implausible.
23.note: A and B are realistic misspellings; good item apart from the consensus tell.

24.free_elimination: Consensus: 'conscient-' in 3 of 4, '-ious' in 2 of 4; A is the only option matching the majority at every position.
24.note: Good distractors; consensus tell still applies.
